stories.title: Muse Glimmer from Meta Superintelligence Labs is now available
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Meta has released Muse Glimmer, its first open model from Superintelligence Labs.
Muse Glimmer is a 30B multimodal model released under the permissive Apache 2.0 license.
It is specifically designed for local coding agents and optimized via Ollama's MLX engine with new DFlash and image input support.

stories.title: Six Chinese AI firms accused of aggressively copying US frontier models
stories.author: Ashley Belanger
bullet_points: Six Chinese AI firms are accused of aggressively copying US frontier AI models.
The US is reportedly urging its AI firms to implement measures to identify and switch Chinese users to less capable models.
The story highlights escalating geopolitical tensions surrounding AI technology and intellectual property.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights the trending status of the 'deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1' model on Hugging Face Benchmarks.
The model is categorized under text-generation and utilizes transformers and safetensors formats.
It is relevant to the conversational AI and large language model (LLM) community.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights the trending status of the meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct model.
It is categorized under text-generation pipelines, indicating its primary function.
The associated tags (transformers, safetensors, llama) confirm its relevance within the modern LLM ecosystem.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: meta-llama/Meta-Llama-3-8B
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights the trending status of the Meta-Llama-3-8B model on Hugging Face.
It is categorized under key AI/ML domains including transformers and text-generation.
The presence of Llama and Meta tags indicates relevance to major large language model developments.

stories.title: NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Lightning
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Lightning is now accessible via Ollama.
It is a 30-billion parameter open model optimized for agentic workflows.
The model is designed for local hardware execution, supporting multi-step tasks and tool calling.

stories.title: Ollama: all aboard open models
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama, a platform for running open models, has secured significant funding.
The company raised $88 million from prominent investors including Y Combinator and Benchmark.
Ollama currently serves a large developer base of 8.9 million users.

stories.title: Faster Gemma 4 on MLX with multi-token prediction
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Gemma 4 inference speed is significantly improved in Ollama 0.31 when running on Apple Silicon.
The performance boost is achieved through the implementation of Multi-Token Prediction (MTP) powered by MLX.
Coding agent performance saw up to a 90% speed increase, as validated by the Aider polyglot benchmark.

stories.title: Ollama's highest performance on Apple Silicon yet with MLX
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama has achieved its peak performance on Apple Silicon using the MLX engine.
The performance improvements translate to higher quality model responses and faster inference speeds.
The updated engine also demonstrates reduced memory consumption when running models.

stories.title: OpenJarvis: a local-first personal AI is now available to run with Ollama
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: OpenJarvis v1.0 is released, providing an open-source framework for personal AI agents.
The key feature is the ability to run these AI agents locally on the user's own hardware.
It features built-in support for Ollama, facilitating local LLM execution.

stories.title: Apple's long-rumored foldable becomes reality with the $2,000 iPhone Duo
stories.author: Ryan Whitwam
bullet_points: Apple is reportedly launching its first foldable device.
The rumored device is named the 'iPhone Duo'.
The expected price point for the foldable is around $2,000.

stories.title: Apple starts preorders for Watch Series 12, Ultra 4 with new Health Sensing System
stories.author: Scharon Harding
bullet_points: Apple has begun preorders for the upcoming Watch Series 12 and Ultra 4 models.
The new wearables feature an enhanced Health Sensing System.
The devices will integrate new capabilities powered by Apple Intelligence.

stories.title: Show-Harness: Just a VLM Agent Can Play Robots
stories.author: Mike Zheng Shou
bullet_points: Introduces Show-Harness, an Embodied Harness designed to bridge the gap between high-level VLM intelligence and low-level robot control.
The system allows Vision-Language Models (VLMs) to 'play' robots by reasoning over discrete semantic action units.
It uses embodiment-specific interpreters to deterministically translate abstract semantic intents into concrete, local robot actions.

stories.title: ConvMem: Convolutional Memory for Long-Context Reasoning
stories.author: Bo Xu
bullet_points: Addresses the context length limitations of Large Language Models (LLMs).
Proposes 'ConvMem,' a convolutional memory approach to improve long-context reasoning.
Aims to overcome the high latency and costly RL training associated with sequential context extension methods.

stories.title: Forgetting Only What Matters: Layer-Selective Unlearning toward Robust LLMs
stories.author: Agoritsa Polyzou
bullet_points: Addresses the critical issue of LLM memorization of sensitive or undesirable training data.
Proposes 'Layer-Selective Unlearning' as a method to selectively forget specific knowledge without full model retraining.
Aims to improve the robustness of unlearning methods against deployment changes like quantization, which often causes knowledge to re-emerge.

stories.title: From Symbolic Perception to Logical Deduction: A Framework for Guiding Language Models in Geometric Reasoning
stories.author: Yi Zhou
bullet_points: Proposes a novel framework to enhance LLMs for geometric reasoning, addressing a major AI challenge.
The framework integrates a 'Geometric Vision Parser' to translate visual diagrams into a format usable by LLMs.
Claims that a specialized LLM setup can achieve performance comparable to complex, computationally intensive Large Multimodal Models (LMMs).

stories.title: DeepSeek v4.1 Flash
stories.author: Liwink
bullet_points: Release of DeepSeek v4.1 Flash, indicating continued advancement in large language models (LLMs).
The model is available on Hugging Face, suggesting it is accessible for community and enterprise use.
The 'Flash' designation implies an emphasis on speed and efficiency, a critical factor in current AI deployment.

stories.title: Claude Desktop support with Ollama
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Claude Desktop now supports Ollama as a third-party gateway.
This integration allows users to run open-source models within the Claude Desktop environment.
It bridges the gap between proprietary AI services and local, open-source LLMs.

stories.title: Improved performance and model support with GGUF
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama 0.30 release introduces performance improvements and enhanced GGUF model compatibility.
The update leverages llama.cpp to broaden model support across various hardware configurations.
It specifically augments Ollama's MLX engine capabilities on Apple silicon.

stories.title: NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Ultra
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Introduction of NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Ultra.
The model is specifically designed for high-throughput reasoning tasks.
It is optimized for supporting long-running agent workflows.

stories.title: Nintendo’s latest Switch 2 update adds VRR support in TV mode
stories.author: Tom Warren
bullet_points: Nintendo's Switch 2 has received a firmware update (23.0.0) that adds Variable Refresh Rate (VRR) support.
VRR functionality was previously promised for the docked mode but was missing upon the console's launch.
The update specifically enables VRR when the Switch 2 is connected to a TV.

stories.title: Volvo XC40 PHEV is back with a new look, better sensors, and Gemini AI
stories.author: Andrew J. Hawkins
bullet_points: Volvo is relaunching the plug-in hybrid (PHEV) version of the XC40 after a three-year hiatus.
The refreshed XC40 will feature a major facelift, enhanced sensor technology, and integration of Gemini AI.
The new model is expected to arrive at dealerships early next year, complementing the existing mild hybrid and electric EX40 models.

stories.title: Automattic CEO Matt Mullenweg placed on leave
stories.author: Emma Roth
bullet_points: Automattic CEO Matt Mullenweg has been placed on a paid leave of absence.
Mullenweg alleges that the company's CFO and board members conspired to place him on leave.
The news originates from a report by 404 Media, detailing internal conflict at the WordPress owner.

stories.title: It’s the year of smartphone price hikes
stories.author: Stevie Bonifield
bullet_points: Apple has implemented price increases across its entire iPhone lineup with the new iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max.
The starting prices for the new flagship models are $1,199 and $1,299, marking a $100 increase.
Price hikes are not limited to the newest models, as older iPhone versions have also seen price adjustments.

stories.title: 4 groups caught using the same Chrome and Windows exploit kit
stories.author: Dan Goodin
bullet_points: Four distinct groups were identified using an identical exploit kit targeting Chrome and Windows.
The vulnerability exploitation highlights the risk associated with patch gaps in operating systems and browsers.
The news suggests that the rapid advancement of AI is accelerating the discovery of new software vulnerabilities.

stories.title: Apple's iPhone 18 Pro adds variable camera aperture and a more powerful chip
stories.author: Samuel Axon
bullet_points: The iPhone 18 Pro is expected to feature a variable camera aperture.
It will be equipped with a more powerful processor chip.
A new thermal management system is included to mitigate overheating issues.

stories.title: IBIB: A Protocol for Measuring Enterprise AI Systems by Serving Route, Not Model Identifier
stories.author: Brian Sathianathan
bullet_points: Proposes a new protocol (IBIB) to measure enterprise AI systems based on their serving route rather than just model identifiers.
Addresses the industry problem where current benchmarks only score advertised model identifiers, ignoring crucial deployment factors like serving route and precision.
The protocol includes a preflight check to verify execution contracts and a scoring rule that incorporates reliability.

stories.title: Semigroup-JEPA: Latent Dynamics Consistency for Zero-Shot Physics Generalization
stories.author: John Sous
bullet_points: Introduces SemiGroup-JEPA (SG-JEPA) to enhance Joint-Embedding Predictive Architecture (JEPA) world models.
Addresses a key limitation of existing JEPA models: the untested capability to learn and generate physically realistic dynamics.
Achieves this by conditioning the temporal model on physics parameters via action-conditioning and joint training.

stories.title: JarvisGUI: Towards Cross-Device GUI Agents with Dynamic Task Composition
stories.author: Haifeng Wang
bullet_points: JarvisGUI addresses the gap in current AI agent evaluation by focusing on cross-device GUI interactions.
The research tackles complex real-world workflows requiring state maintenance and coordination across heterogeneous platforms.
It critiques existing benchmarks for being overly optimistic due to their focus on single-device, static tasks.

stories.title: Fortunate Recall: Ontology-Driven Memory Lifecycle Management for Persistent Coherence in LLMs
stories.author: Eray Tüzün
bullet_points: Addresses the critical issue of unbounded memory growth and retrieval degradation in Large Language Models (LLMs).
Introduces 'Fortunate Recall' (FR), a policy layer that manages memory lifecycle based on fact type.
Classifies personal facts into a behavioral ontology (10+1 categories) to apply tailored retention policies like differential temporal decay.

stories.title: Can Foundation Models Moderate Online Content? Evaluating Instruction- vs. Example-Driven Policy Operationalization
stories.author: Abhisek Dash
bullet_points: The paper addresses the challenge of consistently operationalizing complex online content moderation policies.
It compares two methods for guiding Vision-Language Models (VLMs): instruction-driven (reasoning from precepts) vs. example-driven.
The research evaluates the reliability of foundation models in tackling real-world content moderation tasks.

stories.title: Cross-Model Agreement as a Deployment-Time Reliability Signal for Automatic Polyp Segmentation
stories.author: Jitin Singla
bullet_points: Addresses the critical problem of silent failures in real-time medical AI (polyp segmentation) where ground truth is unavailable during inference.
Introduces Referee-Based Quality Estimation (RBQE), a reference-free framework to measure model reliability by comparing a primary model against an independent 'referee' model.
Validated on a standardized external benchmark, suggesting practical applicability in clinical deployment settings.

stories.title: IBIB: A Protocol for Measuring Enterprise AI Systems by Serving Route, Not Model Identifier
stories.author: Brian Sathianathan
bullet_points: Proposes a new protocol (IBIB) to accurately measure enterprise AI system capabilities.
Addresses the industry flaw of benchmarking based only on model identifiers rather than the actual serving route and configuration.
The protocol includes a preflight check and a reliability-inclusive scoring rule to ensure accurate evaluation.

stories.title: Deep Learning-Based Detection of Electrical Faults and Power Quality Disturbances in Aerospace Power Systems
stories.author: Berker Peköz
bullet_points: Addresses the critical need for monitoring high-frequency electrical networks in More Electric Aircraft (MEA).
Introduces a hardware-aware deep learning framework specifically designed for a 400 Hz aerospace power system.
Focuses on multiclass detection of electrical faults and power quality disturbances using a simulation model based on the Boeing 787 architecture.

stories.title: IBIB: A Protocol for Measuring Enterprise AI Systems by Serving Route, Not Model Identifier
stories.author: Brian Sathianathan
bullet_points: Proposes a new protocol (IBIB) to measure enterprise AI systems based on their serving route rather than just model identifiers.
Highlights that current benchmarks fail to account for crucial deployment factors like serving route, precision, and output contract.
The protocol includes a preflight check to verify execution contracts and a reliability-inclusive scoring rule.

stories.title: Building Multilingual Bridges: Data Mixing as the Pillar of Generalization for In-Language Reasoning
stories.author: Julia Kreutzer
bullet_points: Current reasoning language models exhibit a strong English-centric bias, limiting their utility for non-English speakers.
The research proposes 'Data Mixing' as a core methodology to enhance multilingual capabilities and generalization in language models.
The goal is to advance 'L2 reasoning,' enabling models to reason consistently within the language of the prompt, preserving original intent.

stories.title: ConvMem: Convolutional Memory for Long-Context Reasoning
stories.author: Bo Xu
bullet_points: Addresses the context length limitation in Large Language Models (LLMs).
Proposes 'ConvMem,' a convolutional memory approach to handle long contexts without sequential processing.
Aims to overcome the high latency and costly RL training associated with existing sequential memory methods (like MemAgent).

stories.title: Can Foundation Models Moderate Online Content? Evaluating Instruction- vs. Example-Driven Policy Operationalization
stories.author: Abhisek Dash
bullet_points: The paper investigates the reliability of Foundation Models (specifically VLMs) in moderating complex online content.
It compares two methods for guiding model behavior: instruction-driven (reasoning from policy precepts) vs. example-driven.
The research addresses the critical challenge of consistently operationalizing evolving content moderation policies.

stories.title: Retrofitting Code Using LLMs to Support Exceptional Behavior
stories.author: Milos Gligoric
bullet_points: The research addresses the manual tedium of adding Exception Related Code (ERC) to large software codebases.
A novel task is proposed: retrofitting existing, ERC-less code using Large Language Models (LLMs).
The process leverages Exceptional Behavior Tests (EBTs) as input to guide the LLM in inserting necessary error handling logic.

stories.title: Why Is Video Still So Expensive? A Survey of Inference-Efficiency Mechanisms in Video and Audiovisual LLMs
stories.author: Mounîm A. El Yacoubi
bullet_points: Video Large Language Models (VideoLLMs) are advancing rapidly for video understanding tasks.
The high computational and memory cost of VideoLLMs, which scales with video length, hinders real-time and mobile deployment.
The paper surveys various inference-efficiency mechanisms designed to reduce the operational expense of these models.

stories.title: AI Is Already Better at Coding Than Most Software Developers
stories.author: sylwia-lask
bullet_points: The article discusses the increasing capability of AI in coding tasks.
It posits that coding itself is not the most valuable skill in software development.
This suggests a potential shift in the required skill set for human developers.

stories.title: The Verification Bottleneck in AI-Generated Software
stories.author: kenwalger
bullet_points: AI code generation is accelerating rapidly.
The speed of generation does not guarantee code correctness.
The verification process is identified as a critical bottleneck in AI-driven software development.

stories.title: I let AI write 100% of my code for 30 days. Here's what broke.
stories.author: infoinlet1
bullet_points: The article details an experiment where the author attempted to write 100% of their code using AI for a month.
The focus is on the limitations and failures encountered when relying entirely on AI generation, rather than AI assistance.
This topic is relevant to the current industry discussion around developer productivity and the future role of AI coding tools.

stories.title: Most 'AI Agents' Are Just If-Statements in a Trench Coat
stories.author: james_anderson_h
bullet_points: The article critiques the current implementation of 'AI Agents', suggesting many are overhyped.
The author argues that many existing agents are fundamentally simple, relying on basic conditional logic ('if-statements').
It serves as a critical discussion piece aimed at demystifying the hype surrounding advanced AI agent capabilities.
